title: A small sabbath
hookLine: a phone off, a walk, a meal with no hurry: sabbath can start small
last: REST IS A GIFT, NOT A TEST.

lines: A WHOLE DAY? NOT IN MY LIFE.
cards: Maybe a whole day of rest sounds lovely and impossible. You work weekends. You have small kids who don't know what a sabbath is, or two jobs, or a parent who needs you, or a phone that never stops.
Here's a scene. Jesus's disciples have just come back from traveling and teaching, full of stories, worn out. So many people are crowding around, Mark says, that they don't even have time to eat.
Jesus looks at them and says, in the King James words: "Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while." Not forever. Not a month-long retreat.
A while. So they get into a boat and head for somewhere quiet. Today's word is a sabbath sized for real life.

teach.b: A small sabbath. The full sabbath is a whole day, and those who keep it, Jewish and Christian, treasure it.
But sabbath can also start small: an hour with the phone in a drawer, a walk with nowhere to get to, a meal where nobody hurries. What makes it sabbath isn't the length. It's the stopping.
Now the honest part of Mark's story. The crowd sees where the boat is going and runs around the lake to meet them. By the time they land, a huge crowd is waiting.
Jesus has compassion on them, and teaches them.

teach.h: THE REST WAS SHORT, AND COUNTED.
teach.b: So the rest was short, and interrupted. It still counted. The Gospels show Jesus slipping away more than once, early in the morning or up a mountain, to be alone and pray.
Luke says: "And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed." Short withdrawals, in the middle of a crowded life.
And in Matthew he says: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
Christians today practice small sabbaths in all kinds of ways: a Sunday afternoon with no shopping, a candle lit at dinner, screens off after nine, a daily walk without headphones.
None of these would satisfy a strict sabbath keeper, and they're not meant to replace a full day for those who keep one. They're a door. Often the hard part isn't finding the hour.
It's actually putting the phone down.

how: Alongside or instead of a full day of rest, some Christians keep small sabbaths: an hour of quiet, a screen-free meal, a Sunday afternoon without errands, or a daily walk for prayer.

o: a strict rule against doing any work on Sunday
a real stop for rest, whether a whole day or an hour
a weekly duty to attend a Sunday church service

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: a sabbath only counts if it lasts a whole day
the full day is treasured, but sabbath can start small. the stopping is what counts.
the disciples were so busy they had no time to eat
so Jesus told them to come apart and rest a while.
their rest in the boat went perfectly to plan
the crowd got there first. the rest was short and interrupted, and still counted.

games.q: you and the others are back from traveling, worn out, and the crowd won't let you eat. Jesus turns to you. what does he say?
o: keep going. there's no time to rest.
come apart to a quiet place and rest a while.
games.why: "rest a while," he says, and they take a boat. the crowd runs ahead, and Jesus, moved with compassion, teaches them.

practice: If you're listening on your phone, set it face down or across the room, and notice the pull to check it; just notice, and let it pass. If you pray, say his words to his friends quietly: rest a while.
If you don't, just rest a while.

wordCard.voice: Sabbath: not just a whole day, but a short, real stop in a busy life, an hour, a walk, a meal. The stopping is what makes it holy.

orig.note: Greek: to rest, to refresh. the verb behind rest a while in Mark 6:31.

carryVoice: Your line: stop. it still counts. That was day one hundred twenty-four, and it counts too.
